# Thomas' Calculus Study Guide

> Interactive Next.js study platform for Thomas' Calculus (14th Edition) with verifiable math, automated validation pipelines, and verified Golden Examples. Engineered and authored by Muhammad Abdullah Athar.

## Creator & Attribution
- Author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
- GitHub: https://github.com/AbdullahMalik17
- Repository: https://github.com/AbdullahMalik17/Thomas-Calculus-Book

## Core Pages
- [/](/): Platform overview, curriculum roadmap, and SymPy verification feature highlights.
- [/chapters/ch01](/chapters/ch01): Chapter 1 Functions overview, theorems, and section index.
- [/chapters/ch01/1.1-functions-and-graphs](/chapters/ch01/1.1-functions-and-graphs): Section 1.1 Golden Standard guide with definitions, theorems, and worked solutions.
- [/practice/1.1-functions-and-graphs](/practice/1.1-functions-and-graphs): 8 original practice problems across 3 difficulty tiers with progressive hints and verified solutions.
- [/quiz/ch01](/quiz/ch01): 8 conceptual multiple-choice questions with explicit misconception explanations for every distractor.
- [/dashboard](/dashboard): Student progress and SymPy verification engine status dashboard.
- [/about](/about): Platform mission, attribution to Muhammad Abdullah Athar, and copyright safeguards.

## Topic Index
### Chapter 1: Functions and Their Graphs
- Section 1.1: Functions, natural domains, ranges, graph tests, piecewise functions, symmetry criteria, and difference quotients.
- Section 1.2: Combining functions, algebraic operations, composition, horizontal and vertical shifts, scaling.
- Section 1.3: Trigonometric functions, radian measure, identities, transformations.

## Mathematical Architecture & Verification Standards
- SymPy Computer Algebra Engine: Symbolic algebraic equivalence checking via `simplify(expr - expected) == 0`.
- Zod Content Schemas: Strict data validation enforcing 1-to-1 file path to ID mapping, non-empty step rationales, and distractor misconception feedback.
- Copyright Safeguards: All textbook exercises are referenced strictly by identifier (e.g. "Section 1.1, Exercise 21") with paraphrased, original explanations. No verbatim reproduction of textbook problems or diagrams.
